pageCache.text:
Welcome
We are a creative, forward-thinking Church of England Primary School that aims for 'Life in all its fullness' (the Gospel of John 10:10) to enable each child to flourish through the provision of the best education; academically, morally, socially and spiritually; and by living out our faith in God.
We are delighted to welcome you to St. Paul's Church of England Primary School; a small, village primary school nestled in the heart of Swanley Village, where children explore, learn, create and grow together. We have strong traditional values with a modern outlook and provide a wide range or opportunities for all children and families from our school.
All children are encouraged to be active participants in a dynamic community of learners and inspired to become valued citizens and enthusiastic learners for life. We nurture the development of talent and creative ability through a balanced exposure to academic, cultural, service, social, spiritual and sporting opportunities.
Together the children play sport, create music and stage ambitious productions. They make films, explore the great outdoors and take on physical challenges. They plan dances and social events, debate, develop business ventures, conduct science experiments and solve complex mathematical problems. Together they travel to faraway places, work in disadvantaged communities and work as teams understanding their own individual strengths and abilities.
We take a personal pride in the excellent education St. Paul's offers, as well as the myriad opportunities to engage in extracurricular activities. It is also the perfect size to allow staff to genuinely get to know our families and the children as individuals. As a result, all of our pupils are offered tailored opportunities to be challenged, to become self-reliant, self-aware and achieve the very best according to their gifts.
St. Paul's is part of the Compass Federation, a group of 3 schools that work closely together under an Executive Headteacher and Governing Body.
If our website is your first experience of St. Paul's, then please allow us to extend a warm invitation to you to make a personal visit. This is by far the best way to sample all that we have to offer.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Paul's Church of England Primary School - Academic Results
pageCache.text:
Academic Results
We are very proud of the achievements of our pupils at St Paul’s. Our 2025–2026 statutory assessment results reflect the hard work of our children, staff and families, with strong outcomes across the school.
Early Years
Our Reception children achieved exceptionally strong outcomes, with 93% achieving a Good Level of Development, compared with an estimated national figure of approximately 72%. This continues the strong outcomes seen in Early Years at St Paul’s in recent years.
Phonics
In the Year 1 Phonics Screening Check, 93% of pupils met the expected standard, significantly above the estimated national figure of approximately 82%.
Developing confident, fluent readers remains a central priority at St Paul’s and these results demonstrate the strong foundations our children develop from the beginning of their time at school.
Key Stage 2
Our Year 6 pupils also achieved strong outcomes.
73% achieved the expected standard in reading, writing and mathematics combined, compared with 63% nationally.
20% achieved the higher standard across reading, writing and mathematics combined, compared with approximately 8% nationally.
87% achieved the expected standard in reading, with 40% achieving the higher standard.
93% achieved the expected standard in writing, with 27% working at greater depth.
100% achieved the expected standard in science.
We are particularly pleased that pupils achieving the higher combined standard placed the school within the top 10% nationally in the comparative data contained within our assessment report.
Continuing to Improve
Assessment information is one of a number of ways in which we evaluate the quality of education at St Paul’s. We celebrate these strong outcomes while continuing to identify areas where further improvement is needed.
For example, multiplication-table fluency remains an area of focus. While pupils' wider mathematics attainment was broadly in line with national outcomes, the proportion achieving full marks in the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check was below the estimated national figure. This will therefore remain an important area of development.
As a small school, individual pupils can have a significant impact on percentages from year to year. We therefore consider assessment outcomes alongside pupils' individual starting points, progress, work across the curriculum and the wider development of every child.
We are extremely proud of what our pupils have achieved and remain committed to ensuring that every child at St Paul’s is supported and challenged to flourish.

Current Parents
St. Paul's has a mixed age classroom structure meaning that most year groups are mixed with another. Reception are taught on their own as a group of 15 children. Year 1 and 2 are mixed with 30 children. Year 3/4 and Year 5/6 are mixed, with each class having an average of 32 children.
The curriculum is all the planned activities that we organise in order to promote learning and personal growth and development in preparation for life in modern Britain. It includes not only the formal requirements of the National Curriculum, but also any other activity organised by school, for example, extra-curricular activities and any other activities designed to enrich the experience of the children. There is also a ‘hidden’ element to the curriculum which includes what the children learn from their school environment, the way they are treated and how they are expected to behave.

pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
We hope that your child can be with us in school every day to access learning. However, in exceptional circumstances, this may not always be possible. The following information should help you to ensure that your child can access learning until they can return to lessons at school.
If your child is unable to be in school with us, but is well enough to learn, please follow the following steps:
Send a message to your child's class teacher via Dojo. They will be able to provide you with a suggested timetable for your child’s learning. Please do not hesitate to email or ring the school if you have any questions.
Check our Curriculum overviews on the website.
There are also many helpful websites which your child can access to support them with their learning at home:
Oak Academy has a wide range of lessons available for all curriculum subjects.
BBC Bitesize You will find great videos to support learning across a range of subjects
TTRS Times Tables Rockstars is fantastic for regular practice of times tables.
How can parents support their children with remote learning?
To best support your child’s online learning and progress, we recommend the following:
Make sure your child has the best distraction-free environment possible to learn in.
Check your child’s engagement with their learning. Asking your child the following questions will help you connect with what they are learning:
What have you been learning about today?
Can you show me the learning you are most proud of?
What learning will you be doing next?
Keep in contact with the school, asking questions if things are difficult. We are here to help you.

Admissions & Visits
There is no better way to understand what makes St Paul's special than experiencing it for yourself. The best way to discover our school is to see it in action, meet our wonderful children and staff, and experience the warm, welcoming atmosphere that makes St Paul's such a special place to learn and grow.
We would love to welcome you for a personal tour with a member of our leadership team.
During your visit, you'll have the opportunity to:
Whether you're looking for a Reception place, moving into the area, or simply exploring your options, we'll make sure you leave with all the information you need.
Meet the Headteacher or senior leader.
See children learning.
Visit classrooms.
Find out about our curriculum.
Learn about our values and community.
Ask any questions you have.
What to Expect
We know that choosing a school is a big decision, and visiting a school for the first time can sometimes feel a little daunting. We want you to feel relaxed and welcome from the moment you arrive.
During your visit, you'll have the opportunity to look around the school, see learning in action, meet members of our team and ask any questions you may have.
Our visits usually last around 30–45 minutes, and younger brothers and sisters are very welcome to come along too.
There is absolutely no obligation to apply after your visit. We simply want to give you the opportunity to experience our school, meet our children and staff, and decide whether it feels like the right place for your family.

Extra-Curricular Clubs
We offer a number of after-school clubs for children to attend between 3.15 - 4.15pm. We use our PE and Sports Grant to fund some of the clubs as we believe it is important to provide a variety of clubs for the children to enjoy; children learn, develop and apply skills taught.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Paul's Church of England Primary School - Our Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
Children are inspired to achieve the remarkable at St. Paul’s.
It is partly a question of expectation. We consider every child to be a musician, scientist, mathematician, artist, performer and athlete. We provide children with opportunities to develop their knowledge and skills across the full breadth of the curriculum and encourage them to be the very best they can be.
Our curriculum is underpinned by the National Curriculum for England and the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage framework. We use high-quality published schemes and resources where these support effective curriculum delivery, adapting learning appropriately to meet the needs and experiences of our children.
Our curriculum is carefully planned so that children's knowledge and skills develop progressively over time. Teachers build on prior learning, revisit important knowledge and make meaningful connections between different areas of the curriculum. Our long-term planning ensures that children experience the full breadth of the curriculum while developing increasingly secure knowledge and understanding as they move through the school.
We also help children to understand themselves as learners, develop positive learning behaviours and appreciate the diversity of the world around them, all within the distinctive Christian ethos of St. Paul’s.
Reading and Phonics
We believe that reading is fundamental to children's success across the curriculum.
In Key Stage 1, we use Read Write Inc. as our systematic synthetic phonics programme to teach phonics and early reading.
Children in Key Stage 1 also learn through play and continuous provision. They are given carefully planned learning challenges throughout the week, with skilled adults supporting, questioning and extending their learning.
Power of Reading is used across the school to support high-quality teaching of reading and writing. Children encounter carefully chosen, high-quality texts that help develop their reading, vocabulary, comprehension, writing and enjoyment of literature.
Reading is taught through a range of approaches appropriate to children's age and stage. Children have regular opportunities to read and discuss texts, develop their reading skills and enjoy books together.
Parents and carers are encouraged to support reading at home, helping us to develop children who read confidently and, importantly, love reading.
An ambitious and inclusive curriculum
Our curriculum is ambitious for every child.
We strive to provide a broad and balanced education in a happy, caring and stimulating environment in which children can develop confidence, independence and a strong sense of self-worth.
Teachers use adaptive teaching, appropriate resources and reasonable adjustments to enable pupils, including those with SEND, to access and participate successfully in the full curriculum.
Further information about our approach to supporting children with SEND can be found on our Inclusion & SEND page.
Our Curriculum Aims
By learning together, we aim to:
develop responsible, confident and independent young people;
widen children's experiences and raise aspirations;
celebrate creativity, achievement and individuality; and
Preparing children for life in modern Britain
At St. Paul’s, we take seriously our responsibility to prepare children for life in modern Britain.
The fundamental British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs are promoted through our curriculum, Christian ethos and wider school life.
Subjects including Religious Education and PSHE, together with collective worship and opportunities across the wider curriculum, enable children to explore these values and understand how they apply to their own lives.
We want children to develop the knowledge, confidence and understanding they need to participate positively in their communities and to respect and value people whose experiences, backgrounds, beliefs and perspectives may be different from their own.
Religious Education
Religious Education is an important part of our curriculum and reflects the distinctive Christian character of St. Paul’s.
Through RE, children develop their knowledge and understanding of Christianity and other religions and worldviews. They are encouraged to consider important questions about faith, belief, meaning and how people live, while developing respect for the beliefs and perspectives of others.
Parents and carers have a statutory right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education.
We encourage any parent or carer considering withdrawal to speak to the Head of School so that the curriculum and implications of withdrawal can be discussed.
Learning beyond the classroom
We believe that children's education should extend beyond individual lessons and the classroom.
We provide opportunities for children to broaden their experiences through educational visits, visitors, music, art, sport, performances, outdoor learning and other enrichment opportunities.
These experiences help children to make connections with their learning, encounter opportunities beyond their immediate community and develop their interests and talents.
Our aim is to raise aspirations and enable children to discover things they enjoy, things they are good at and possibilities for their future.
What does my child learn?
Our Long Term Plans set out the curriculum content taught across the school and show how learning is organised throughout the academic year.
They provide information about the learning children encounter across English, Mathematics, Science, Religious Education and the wider curriculum, including History, Geography, Art, Design & Technology, Computing, Music, PE, Languages and PSHE.
For example, our Year 3/4 rolling programme identifies specific learning in each subject across the year, including units in Science, RE, History, Geography, Computing, Art, DT, Music, PE, French and PSHE. The second cycle ensures children encounter different content, including Roman Britain, Anglo-Saxons and Scots, Vikings, rivers, migration and natural resources.
Please select the relevant Long Term Plan below to see what children will learn.
Our mixed-age curriculum operates on a rolling programme. This ensures that children experience the full breadth of the curriculum during their time within each mixed-age phase without unnecessarily repeating the same curriculum content.
Further information about children's current learning and ways parents and carers can support learning at home can be found on our individual class pages.
If you would like further information about the curriculum taught at St. Paul’s, please contact the school office.

Forest School
Forest School is about using the outdoors to promote confidence, self-esteem and independence. At St. Paul's we are passionate about developing the whole child, not just their academic ability. The benefits of Forest School to the children are many and include improved confidence, behaviour, concentration, independence, resilience, creativity and teamwork.
Our Forest School is led by Mr Manning who is fully qualified Level 3 Forest School Leaders.
Forest Schools continues the ethos of an already nurturing environment within St. Paul's and provides inclusion for all children. Forest Schools encourages children to develop their communication and social skills, alongside developing resilience, independence and perseverance outside of the classroom environment. Each week the children will engage in team building activities where they must work in pairs or groups to complete their tasks, through working together it will help support their self –esteem, boost their confidence and emotional well-being which can then be transferred back into school life. Praise and encouragement are in abundance from both peers and adults throughout each session.

Arbor Parent App
At St. Paul’s, we use Arbor as our school information and communication system. The Arbor Parent App is the main way that we communicate with parents and carers and enables you to access important information about your child in one place.
Through Arbor, parents and carers can:
receive messages and important updates from the school;
view information relating to their child;
book and pay for school meals;
make payments for trips and other activities;
sign up for clubs and activities;
book parents’ evening appointments; and
keep contact and personal information up to date.
We strongly encourage all parents and carers to download and use the Arbor Parent App, as this helps ensure that you receive important school information promptly.
Keeping Your Details Up to Date
Arbor uses the contact information held by the school. It is therefore essential that we have your current email address and mobile telephone number.
If your contact details change, please update them through Arbor where possible or contact the School Office so that we can amend our records.
All personal information is handled securely and in accordance with our data protection responsibilities.
Getting Started with the Arbor Parent App
The Arbor Parent App is available free of charge for Apple and Android devices.
Search for “Arbor” in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store and download the Arbor Parent App.
Use the email address that you have registered with the school.
Follow the instructions within the app to create or access your account.
Once logged in, you will be able to see the information and services available for your child.
If you experience any difficulties accessing Arbor, please contact the School Office, who will be happy to help.
We recommend enabling notifications for the Arbor Parent App so that you do not miss important messages or updates from the school.
